text: If the function $f(x)=\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )^{2x};x>0$ attains the maximum value at $x=\frac{1}{\mathrm{e}}$ then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $x>0$, $\ln f(x)=-2x\ln x$, so

$\dfrac{f^{'}(x)}{f(x)}=-2(\ln x+1)$

As $f(x)>0$, $f^{'}(x)>0$ for $0<x<\dfrac{1}{e}$ and $f^{'}(x)<0$ for $x>\dfrac{1}{e}$: $f$ is increasing on $\left (0,\dfrac{1}{e}\right ]$ and has its maximum at $x=\dfrac{1}{e}$.

Since $π>e$, $\dfrac{1}{π}<\dfrac{1}{e}$, so $f\left (\dfrac{1}{π}\right )<f\left (\dfrac{1}{e}\right )$, where $f\left (\dfrac{1}{π}\right )=π^{2/π}$ and $f\left (\dfrac{1}{e}\right )=e^{2/e}$:

$π^{2/π}<e^{2/e}$

Raising both positive sides to the power $\dfrac{eπ}{2}$:

$π^{e}<e^{π}$

So (D) is true and (A) is false. The same monotonicity rules out (B) and (C): $f\left (\dfrac{1}{2π}\right )<f\left (\dfrac{1}{e}\right )$ gives $(2π)^{e}<e^{2π}$, and $\dfrac{1}{2e}<\dfrac{1}{π}$ gives $f\left (\dfrac{1}{2e}\right )<f\left (\dfrac{1}{π}\right )$, i.e. $(2e)^{π}<π^{2e}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text: Let $\mathrm{A}=\{1,2,3,4,5\}$. Let $\mathrm{R}$ be a relation on $\mathrm{A}$ defined by $x\mathrm{R}y$ if and only if $4x\leq 5\mathrm{y}$. Let $\mathrm{m}$ be the number of elements in $\mathrm{R}$ and $\mathrm{n}$ be the minimum number of elements from $\mathrm{A}\times \mathrm{A}$ that are required to be added to R to make it a symmetric relation. Then m + n is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} A=\{1,2,3,4,5\} \\ xRy⇔4x\leq 5y \\ 4x\leq 5y\Rightarrow \dfrac{x}{y}\leq \dfrac{5}{4}\Rightarrow \dfrac{x}{y}\leq 1.25 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} R=\{(1,2),(1,3),(1,4),(1,5),(1,1),(2,2),(2,3),(2,4), \\ (2,5),(3,3),(3,4),(3,5),(4,4),(4,5),(5,4),(5,5)\} \\ \therefore \quad n(R)=m=16 \end{array}$

text: $\lim _{n\to \infty }\frac{\left (1^{2}-1\right )(n-1)+\left (2^{2}-2\right )(n-2)+\cdots +\left ((n-1)^{2}-(n-1)\right )\cdot 1}{(1^{3}+2^{3}+\cdots \cdots +n^{3})-(1^{2}+2^{2}+\cdots \cdots +n^{2})}$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{n\to \infty }\frac{(1^{2}-1)(n-1)+(2^{2}-2)(n-2)+...+\left ((n-1)^{2}-(n-1)\right )\times 1}{(1^{3}+2^{3}+...+n^{3})-(1^{2}+2^{2}+...+n^{2})}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Numerator}=\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n-1}\left ((r-1)^{2}-(r-1)\right )(n-r) \\ =\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n-1}(r-1)(r-2)(n-r) \\ =\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n-1}-r^{3}+(n+3)r^{2}-(2+3n)r+2n \end{array}$

We will take term with the greatest power of $n$

$=\frac{-1}{4}n^{4}+\frac{1}{3}n^{4}=\frac{1}{12}n^{4}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Denominator}=\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}r^{3}-\sum\limits _{r=1}^{n}r^{2} \\ =\left (\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}\right )^{2}-\left (\dfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}\right ) \end{array}$

Greatest power of $n$ is $\frac{n^{4}}{4}$

$\lim _{n\to \infty }\frac{\frac{1}{12}n^{4}}{\frac{n4}{4}}=\frac{1}{3}$

text: If three letters can be posted to any one of the 5 different addresses, then the probability that the three letters are posted to exactly two addresses is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Each of the 3 letters can go to any of the 5 addresses, so the total number of ways is $5^{3}=125$.

The 2 addresses that receive letters are chosen in ${}^{5}C_{2}=10$ ways.

Each letter then goes to one of these 2 addresses in $2^{3}=8$ ways, of which 2 put all three letters at a single address; so both chosen addresses receive letters in $8-2=6$ ways.

$P=\dfrac{10\times 6}{125}=\dfrac{60}{125}=\dfrac{12}{25}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text: Let $⃗{a}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k},⃗{b}=((⃗{a}\times (\hat{i}+\hat{j}))\times \hat{i})\times \hat{i}$. Then the square of the projection of $⃗{a}$ on $⃗{b}$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{lllllll} ⃗{a}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k} \\ ⃗{b}=((⃗{a}\times (\hat{i}+\hat{j}))\times \hat{i})\times \hat{i} \\ ⃗{a}\times (\hat{i}+\hat{j})=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \end{array}\right | \\ =\hat{i}(1)-\hat{j}(1)+\hat{k}(2-1) \\ =\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{lllllll} (⃗{a}\times (\hat{i}+\hat{j}))\times \hat{i}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right | \\ =\hat{i}(0)-\hat{j}(-1)+\hat{k}(1) \\ =\hat{j}+\hat{k} \end{array}$

$\left ((\vec{a}\times (\hat{i}+\hat{j})\times \hat{i}\right )\times \hat{i}=\left |\begin{array}{lll} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right |$

$\begin{array}{ll} =\hat{i}(0)-\hat{j}(-1)+\hat{k}(-1) \\ ⃗{b}= & \hat{j}-\hat{k} \end{array}$

Projection of $⃗{a}$ on $⃗{b}=\frac{⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b}}{|⃗{b}|}$

$=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}$

Square of projection $=2$

text: Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle. A new triangle is formed by joining the middle points of all sides of the triangle $ABC$ and the same process is repeated infinitely many times. If $\mathrm{P}$ is the sum of perimeters and $Q$ is the sum of areas of all the triangles formed in this process, then :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$△ABC$ is an equilateral triangle having side $=a$ unit

Now, perimeter $=$ sum of all sides $=3a$

Area $=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^{2}$

Now, in $△DEF,DE=\frac{a}{2}=EF=DF$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Perimeter}=3\times \dfrac{a}{2}=\dfrac{3a}{2} \\ \text{Area}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\times \left (\dfrac{a}{2}\right )^{2}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}a^{2}}{16} \end{array}$

Now, $P=3a+\frac{3a}{2}+\frac{3a}{4}+\cdots$

$Q=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{16}a^{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{64}a^{2}+\cdots$

$P=\frac{3a}{1-\frac{1}{2}}=3a\times 2\Rightarrow P=6a\text{.... (i)}$

$Q=\frac{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^{2}}{1-\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{4}{3}\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^{2}Q=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}a^{2}\text{.... (ii)}$

From equation (i) & (ii)

$\begin{array}{l} P=6a \\ Q=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}a^{2} \\ Q=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\times \dfrac{P^{2}}{36} \\ P^{2}=36\sqrt{3}Q \end{array}$

text: Suppose the solution of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{(2+α)x-βy+2}{βx-2αy-(βγ-4α)}$ represents a circle passing through origin. Then the radius of this circle is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Cross-multiplying,

$βxdy-2αydy-(βγ-4α)dy=(2+α)xdx-βydx+2dx.$

Grouping $β(xdy+ydx)=βd(xy)$ and integrating:

$βxy-αy^{2}-(βγ-4α)y=\left (1+\dfrac{α}{2}\right )x^{2}+2x+C,$

so the solution curves are

$\left (1+\dfrac{α}{2}\right )x^{2}+αy^{2}-βxy+2x+(βγ-4α)y+C=0.$

For a circle the $xy$ term must vanish and the coefficients of $x^{2}$ and $y^{2}$ must be equal: $β=0$ and $1+\dfrac{α}{2}=α$, so $α=2$. Passing through the origin gives $C=0$.

With $β=0$ and $α=2$: $2x^{2}+2y^{2}+2x-8y=0$, i.e. $x^{2}+y^{2}+x-4y=0$.

The centre is $\left (-\dfrac{1}{2},2\right )$, so the radius is $\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4}+4}=\dfrac{\sqrt{17}}{2}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text: A software company sets up m number of computer systems to finish an assignment in 17 days. If 4 computer systems crashed on the start of the second day, 4 more computer systems crashed on the start of the third day and so on, then it took 8 more days to finish the assignment. The value of $\mathrm{m}$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the value of $\mathrm{m}$, we need to formulate the problem using some basic concepts of arithmetic progression and work. Let's first understand the nature of the problem:

Initially, there are $\mathrm{m}$ computers, and it is estimated that with these $\mathrm{m}$ computers, the assignment can be completed in 17 days.

However, due to the crash of 4 computers every day starting from the second day onward, the total time taken extends by 8 days, making it 25 days in total.

To begin with, let's define the total work (W) in terms of the number of computers and days:

The total work (W) is given by:

The amount of work completed each day with $\mathrm{m}$ computers for 17 days:

$W=17m$

When computers crash, the number of working computers each day forms an arithmetic sequence. On the first day, there are $\mathrm{m}$ computers. On the second day, there are $\mathrm{m}-4$ computers, on the third day, there are $\mathrm{m}-8$ computers, and so on. We need to sum this series until 25 days are completed.

This can be formulated as:

Total work done over 25 days with decrement in the number of computers:

$W=m+(m-4)+(m-8)+\ldots +[m-4\times (n-1)]$

where $n$ is the number of days. Here, $n=25$.

Notice that we form an arithmetic series where the first term (a) is $\mathrm{m}$ and the common difference (d) is -4. The sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic series is:

$S_{n}=\frac{n}{2}[2a+(n-1)d]$

Plugging in the values:

$S_{25}=\frac{25}{2}[2m+(25-1)(-4)]$

$S_{25}=\frac{25}{2}[2m-96]$

$S_{25}=\frac{25}{2}[2m-96]=25(m-48)$

This work should be equivalent to the work calculated earlier, so:

$17m=25(m-48)$

Solving for $\mathrm{m}$:

$17m=25m-1200$

$8m=1200$

$m=150$

Thus, the value of $\mathrm{m}$ is equal to:

Option C: 150
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift

text: Suppose for a differentiable function $h,h(0)=0,h(1)=1$ and $h^{'}(0)=h^{'}(1)=2$. If $g(x)=h(\mathrm{e}^{x})\mathrm{e}^{h(x)}$, then $g^{'}(0)$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine $g^{'}(0)$, we start by applying the chain rule and product rule to find the derivative of the given function $g(x)=h(\mathrm{e}^{x})\mathrm{e}^{h(x)}$.

The product rule states that if we have two functions $u(x)$ and $v(x)$, then the derivative of their product is given by:

$(u(x)v(x))^{'}=u^{'}(x)v(x)+u(x)v^{'}(x)$

Let's denote $u(x)=h(\mathrm{e}^{x})$ and $v(x)=\mathrm{e}^{h(x)}$.

First, we need to find $u^{'}(x)$ and $v^{'}(x)$. Using the chain rule, we find:

$u^{'}(x)=\frac{d}{dx}h(\mathrm{e}^{x})=h^{'}(\mathrm{e}^{x})\cdot \frac{d}{dx}(\mathrm{e}^{x})=h^{'}(\mathrm{e}^{x})\cdot \mathrm{e}^{x}$

Now, the derivative of $v(x)$ is:

$v^{'}(x)=\frac{d}{dx}(\mathrm{e}^{h(x)})=\mathrm{e}^{h(x)}\cdot h^{'}(x)$

Using the product rule, we get the derivative of $g(x)$:

$g^{'}(x)=u^{'}(x)v(x)+u(x)v^{'}(x)$

Substituting $u(x)$, $v(x)$, $u^{'}(x)$, and $v^{'}(x)$ into the above expression, we get:

$g^{'}(x)=(h^{'}(\mathrm{e}^{x})\mathrm{e}^{x})\mathrm{e}^{h(x)}+(h(\mathrm{e}^{x}))\left (\mathrm{e}^{h(x)}h^{'}(x)\right )$

Next, we need to evaluate this at $x=0$:

First, we know that:

$h(0)=0$

$h(1)=1$

$h^{'}(0)=2$

$h^{'}(1)=2$

Substituting $x=0$ into the expressions, we get:

$u(0)=h(\mathrm{e}^{0})=h(1)=1$

$v(0)=\mathrm{e}^{h(0)}=\mathrm{e}^{0}=1$

$u^{'}(0)=h^{'}(\mathrm{e}^{0})\mathrm{e}^{0}=h^{'}(1)\cdot 1=2$

$v^{'}(0)=\mathrm{e}^{h(0)}h^{'}(0)=\mathrm{e}^{0}\cdot 2=2$

Therefore, evaluating $g^{'}(0)$:

$g^{'}(0)=(u^{'}(0)v(0))+(u(0)v^{'}(0))$

$g^{'}(0)=(2\cdot 1)+(1\cdot 2)$

$g^{'}(0)=2+2=4$

Thus, the value of $g^{'}(0)$ is 4, which corresponds to Option A.

solution.body:
Given $0\leq r\leq n$. If $\left (n+1r+1\right ):\left (nr\right ):\left (n-1r-1\right )=55:35:21$, then we are to determine the value of $2n+5r$.

Step-by-Step Solution:

Write the given proportions involving binomial coefficients:

$\frac{n+1}{r+1}\times \left (nr\right ):\left (nr\right ):\frac{r}{n}\times \left (nr\right )=55:35:21$

Simplify the proportions:

$\frac{n+1}{r+1}=\frac{55}{35}\text{and}\frac{n}{r}=\frac{35}{21}$

From the simplified ratios, we establish the following two equations:

$\frac{n+1}{r+1}=\frac{11}{7}\Rightarrow 7(n+1)=11(r+1)\Rightarrow 7n-11r=4\text{.... (1)}$

$\frac{n}{r}=\frac{5}{3}\Rightarrow 3n=5r\Rightarrow 3n-5r=0\text{.... (2)}$

Solve equations (1) and (2) simultaneously:

From equation (2), solve for $n$:

$3n=5r\Rightarrow n=\frac{5r}{3}$

Substitute $n$ into equation (1):

$7\left (\frac{5r}{3}\right )-11r=4\Rightarrow \frac{35r}{3}-11r=4$

$\frac{35r-33r}{3}=4\Rightarrow \frac{2r}{3}=4\Rightarrow 2r=12\Rightarrow r=6$

Substituting $r$ back to find $n$:

$n=\frac{5\times 6}{3}=10$

Compute $2n+5r$:

$2n+5r=2\times 10+5\times 6=20+30=50$

Thus, the value of $2n+5r$ is 50.

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{ll} f(x) & =\left [\dfrac{x}{2}+3\right ]-[\sqrt{x}] \\ \qquad =\left [\dfrac{x}{2}\right ]-[\sqrt{x}]+3 \end{array}$

Critical points where $f(x)$ might change behaviours when $\frac{x}{2}\in$ integer and $\sqrt{x}\in$ integer

$\Rightarrow$ Critical points,

$\begin{array}{l} f(0)=3 \\ f\left (0^{+}\right )=3 \\ f\left (1^{-}\right )=3 \\ f\left (1^{+}\right )=2 \\ f\left (2^{-}\right )=2 \\ f\left (2^{+}\right )=3 \\ f\left (3^{+}\right )=f\left (3^{-}\right )=3=f\left (4^{+}\right )=f\left (4^{-}\right )=f\left (5^{+}\right )=f\left (5^{-}\right ) \\ f\left (6^{-}\right )=3 \\ f\left (6^{+}\right )=4 \\ f\left (7^{-}\right )=f\left (7^{+}\right )=4 \\ f\left (8^{-}\right )=4 \\ f(8)=5 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow f(x)\text{is not continuous at} \\ x=1,2,6,8 \\ \Rightarrow \sum\limits _{a\in S}a=1+2+6+8 \\ =17 \end{array}$

text: If the solution $y(x)$ of the given differential equation $(e^{y}+1)\cos x\mathrm{d}x+\mathrm{e}^{y}\sin x\mathrm{d}y=0$ passes through the point $\left (\frac{π}{2},0\right )$, then the value of $e^{y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )}$ is equal to $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given the differential equation

$(e^{y}+1)\cos xdx+e^{y}\sin xdy=0,$

we aim to find the value of $e^{y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )}$ given that the solution $y(x)$ passes through the point $\left (\frac{π}{2},0\right )$.

First, we recognize that the differential equation can be rearranged as:

$d(e^{y}\sin x)+\cos xdx=0.$

Integrating this expression, we obtain:

$e^{y}\sin x+\sin x=C,$

where $C$ is a constant. Given that the solution passes through the point $\left (\frac{π}{2},0\right )$, we substitute these values into the equation to find $C$:

$e^{0}\sin \left (\frac{π}{2}\right )+\sin \left (\frac{π}{2}\right )=C\Rightarrow 1+1=C\Rightarrow C=2.$

Thus, the equation simplifies to:

$e^{y}\sin x+\sin x=2.$

We now need to determine the value of $e^{y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )}$. Substituting $x=\frac{π}{6}$ into the equation, we get:

$\left (e^{y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )}+1\right )\cdot \sin \left (\frac{π}{6}\right )=2.$

Since $\sin \left (\frac{π}{6}\right )=\frac{1}{2}$, the equation becomes:

$\left (e^{y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )}+1\right )\cdot \frac{1}{2}=2\Rightarrow e^{y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )}+1=4\Rightarrow e^{y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )}=3.$

Therefore, the value of $e^{y\left (\frac{π}{6}\right )}$ is $3$.

text: Let $α,β$ be roots of $x^{2}+\sqrt{2}x-8=0$. If $\mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{n}}=α^{\mathrm{n}}+β^{\mathrm{n}}$, then $\frac{\mathrm{U}_{10}+\sqrt{2}\mathrm{U}_{9}}{2\mathrm{U}_{8}}$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since $α$ and $β$ are roots of $x^{2}+\sqrt{2}x-8=0$,

$α^{2}+\sqrt{2}α=8,β^{2}+\sqrt{2}β=8.$

Multiplying the first by $α^{8}$ and the second by $β^{8}$:

$α^{10}+\sqrt{2}α^{9}=8α^{8},β^{10}+\sqrt{2}β^{9}=8β^{8}.$

Adding the two,

$U_{10}+\sqrt{2}U_{9}=8U_{8}.$

Therefore

$\frac{U_{10}+\sqrt{2}U_{9}}{2U_{8}}=\frac{8U_{8}}{2U_{8}}=4.$

Hence, the answer is 4.

text:
If the system of equations

$\begin{array}{l} 2x+7y+λz=3 \\ 3x+2y+5z=4 \\ x+μy+32z=-1 \end{array}$

has infinitely many solutions, then $(λ-μ)$ is equal to $______$ :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 6th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine if the system of equations:

$\begin{array}{l} 2x+7y+λz=3 \\ 3x+2y+5z=4 \\ x+μy+32z=-1 \end{array}$

has infinitely many solutions, we must use Cramer's rule.

The determinants are calculated as follows:

$\begin{array}{ll} \Delta  & =-2λ+3λμ-10μ-509 \\ \Delta _{1} & =2λ+3λμ-15μ-739 \\ \Delta _{2} & =-7λ-7 \\ \Delta _{3} & =μ+39 \end{array}$

To have infinitely many solutions, the determinants must satisfy:

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta =\Delta _{1}=\Delta _{2}=\Delta _{3}=0 \end{array}$

Solving these equations, we find:

$λ=-1,μ=-39$

Thus, the value of $λ-μ$ is:

$λ-μ=38$
